title: feedback:rebootstrap cannot run when ai-runs/ is cleared, so the documented recovery is circular
body:
`npm run feedback:status` fails closed and names a recovery command that cannot run when
`ai-runs/` has been cleared, so the feedback ledger has no reachable way back.

REPRODUCED IN THIS CHECKOUT (2026-08-31, at commit 76e62f80)

  $ npm run feedback:status
  accepted feedback compile is missing or corrupt; restore its ignored artifacts or run
  npm run feedback:rebootstrap
  -> exit 1

  $ npm run feedback:rebootstrap
  feedback:compile - bootstrap cohort: 0 verified reports, 0 crawl findings, 0 hot spots.
  Wrote ai-runs/feedback/20260831T145156Z/hotspots.json
  Wrote ai-runs/feedback/20260831T145156Z/hotspots.md
  Wrote ai-runs/feedback/20260831T145156Z/retention.json
  Wrote ai-runs/feedback/20260831T145156Z/report-manifest.json
  ai-runs/latest-cycle.json is missing
  -> exit 1

  $ npm run feedback:status
  accepted feedback compile is missing or corrupt; restore its ignored artifacts or run
  npm run feedback:rebootstrap
  -> exit 1

Identical error, identical advice. The loop is closed.

WHY IT CANNOT BE ESCAPED

The `feedback_acceptance` marker in AI_LOOP_STATE.md points at
`ai-runs/feedback/20260822T154750Z/{hotspots,report-manifest}.json`. Those are IGNORED
artifacts (.gitignore:14 `ai-runs/`) and this checkout no longer has them, so
`loadAcceptedFeedbackBundle` returns null and `authoritativePolicy` throws
(bin/feedback.ts:147).

`--rebootstrap` is the documented escape and its guards are satisfied: a committed
accepted compile exists, and its bundle is genuinely invalid. It recompiles a zero-delta
baseline and writes four good artifacts — then dies at bin/feedback.ts:215 because
`ai-runs/latest-cycle.json` does not exist.

That file is ALSO an ignored artifact under the same `ai-runs/` rule, lost in the same
event, and it is only ever written by a loop.sh-driven cycle (src/ai-loop.ts, loop.sh).
So the recovery for "the ignored feedback artifacts are gone" itself requires a different
ignored artifact that is gone for exactly the same reason.

Closing the circle: running a cycle to regenerate it needs `loop.sh`, which needs one of
codex/claude/gemini on PATH. `npm run doctor` here reports "none of codex, claude, gemini
is on PATH" — this repo's own dev loop is currently driven by an interactive agent, which
never writes latest-cycle.json.

Rebootstrap IS covered by tests/regression/feedback_rebootstrap_cli.test.ts, so this is
not an untested command. The untested state is the one that actually happened: `ai-runs/`
cleared wholesale rather than just the feedback bundle.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT

Either make `--rebootstrap` self-sufficient — it is recovery, so it should not require
per-cycle metadata it can synthesise or skip — or have it fail with the truth
("recovery also needs ai-runs/latest-cycle.json, which only a loop.sh cycle writes")
instead of pointing back at itself. The first is better: a recovery path that depends on
the machinery being recovered is not a recovery path.

Worth checking at the same time whether any other fail-closed message names a remedy
whose own preconditions live in ai-runs/.

SEVERITY NOTE

Not blocking the dev loop today: charter step 6 is a prompted-agent step, the outer gates
(crawl:smoke, health, integrity drift) are the bar and are unaffected, and two full cycles
landed green today with feedback:status red throughout. The cost is that the feedback
compiler — the thing that ranks what to work on next — is unavailable until someone
restores an artifact by hand.

evidence.summary: status advises rebootstrap; rebootstrap dies on ai-runs/latest-cycle.json, itself an ignored artifact lost in the same event
